item.title: Lego Robotics for Elementary Students — Sat Sep 12, 1:00 PM — RecRoom
item.description: LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. Kids will explore: • Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components • Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect) • Testing, debugging, and iterating designs • Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas Details: • 60-minute session • Small-group format • No prior experience required Community Spons

item.title: 2Pac Revisited: A Concert Fundraiser for Family Healing Center — Sat Sep 12, 5:30 PM — Montclair Brewery
item.description: Welcome to 2Pac Revisited!!! In a world where celebrity & fame can distract us from real issues in our society, there are those who transcend beyond recognition. Many of those challenges deal with mental health, especially in the black & brown communities. Tupac Shakur, a revolution artist, challenged society & its people in such a way; his work continues to be reexamined, celebrated, & taught even at a higher learning level. This event is dedicated the Tupac Shakur’s not to glorify his fame, but to his humanity, as a community leader, entrepreneur, & his love for people. This event will be raising both awareness & fundraising for a mental health-based organization called Family Health Care. There mission states: Our mission is to empower people, build strong families and transform communities through a team of caring professionals who are rooted in faith, hope, and love. 2Pac Revisited will be presented in 3 Parts. item.title: 80's Summer Movie Series — Sun Sep 13, 8:00 AM — Bellevue Theatre
item.description: Step back into the 80s! To celebrate their 40-year reunion, the Montclair High School Class of 1986 is bringing four classic films back to the big screen at the historic Bellevue Theatre. The Lineup (Sundays at 2:30 PM / Doors at 2:00 PM): July 26: Trading Places August 9: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom August 30: Footloose September 13: Ferris Bueller’s Day Off The Cause: Proceeds support the MHS Class of 1986 Scholarship, administered through the Montclair Scholarship Fund. Created entirely through alumni donations, the Class of 1986 is proudly one of only two MHS graduating classes to establish a named, class-specific scholarship, supporting graduating Mounties for more than a decade. Tickets: $30 (includes popcorn!). Note: Seating is limited, and tickets must be purchased in advance online—none will be sold at the door. Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and feel good. Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion.
